quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Is it safe to use the front brake?

options.text: Only when you need to stop quickly.
Only on slippery roads.
No, it is not as effective as the rear brake.
Yes, if you use it correctly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if you use it correctly.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and is safe to use when used correctly.

questions.question: Your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings. What should you do?

options.text: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Grip the handlebars tightly and speed up to get past the hazard.
Ride in a zigzag motion.
Ride on the shoulder instead of over the grooves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay relaxed, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is usually not dangerous. Simply relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: What happens if you shift into a lower gear while going too fast?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
Your horn may sound.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may skid.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light may turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while moving too fast, your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid. This can cause you to lose control. Always slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: What does making eye contact with another driver mean?

options.text: They see you.
They will definitely yield to you.
It does not mean they see you.
It is a waste of effort.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume that eye contact means a driver will yield to you. A driver can look directly at you and still fail to notice you.

questions.question: When riding in a group and passing another vehicle, what is the best method?

options.text: Wait for one rider to finish passing before the next rider begins to pass.
Have several riders pass the vehicle at the same time.
Have the last rider wave to signal no other motorcycles are coming.
Pass in a staggered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for one rider to finish passing before the next rider begins to pass.
questions.explanation: Riders should pass one at a time. Each rider must complete their pass and return to the group before the next rider passes.

questions.question: What is a major effect of drinking alcohol?

options.text: Better riding ability.
Slowed body functions.
Increased nervousness.
Increased alertness.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowed body functions.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows down body functions, both physical and mental. It impairs your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: A driver is tailgating you. What should you do?

options.text: Ignore them.
Change lanes safely and let them pass.
Speed up.
Leave the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes safely and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best solution is to change lanes safely and let the tailgater pass. Speeding up may only encourage them to tailgate at a higher speed.

questions.question: What headlight should you use when riding in fog?

options.text: High beam.
Low beam.
No lights.
Alternate between low and high beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Do not use your high beams around other vehicles.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane to see better before passing a vehicle on the left?

options.text: In the left portion of your lane.
In the right portion of your lane.
In the center portion of your lane.
Standing up on your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of your lane when preparing to pass. This improves your view and makes you more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How can you prevent other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: Give other drivers dirty looks.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves less space on either side. This makes it harder for drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: You will ______ hear a tire going flat.

options.text: Always
Usually
Frequently
Seldom

questions.correctAnswerText: Seldom
questions.explanation: You will rarely hear a tire going flat. Instead, you will notice changes in how the motorcycle handles.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:

options.text: Happen at night.
Are caused by bald tires.
Occur at speeds above 55 mph.
Involve inexperienced riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Involve inexperienced riders.
questions.explanation: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen in daylight at low speeds.

questions.question: A skidding rear tire:

options.text: Is not serious.
Eliminates your ability to change direction.
Will usually correct itself.
Is only a concern if the front tire is also skidding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Eliminates your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel and removes your ability to steer. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Help you avoid surface hazards.
Provide you with an escape route.
Welcome other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Welcome other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position keeps you out of blind spots, helps you see and be seen, avoids hazards, and gives you an escape route. Position yourself to discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's total braking power can the front brake supply?

options.text: About 10 percent
About 25 percent
About 50 percent
About 70 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: About 70 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When an operator's left arm is extended straight out to the left, it means the operator:

options.text: Plans to turn left.
Is about to stop.
Plans to turn right.
Is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Operators use hand signals instead of turn signals to show their intentions. A left arm extended straight out means the operator plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: To control a motorcycle properly, you should:

options.text: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
Sit far enough back on the seat that you can keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to steer, not to hold yourself up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not support your body. Keep your arms slightly bent. Press your knees against the gas tank and keep your feet on the footrests for balance.

questions.question: When should the front brake be used?

options.text: Any time the rider is slowing or stopping
Only when slowing or stopping on slippery roads
Only when slowing or stopping in an emergency
Only when slowing or stopping in traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time the rider is slowing or stopping
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Brightly-colored helmets:

options.text: May make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
Can be distracting.
Don't help to improve a rider's visibility.
Are not permitted.

questions.correctAnswerText: May make it easier for the wearer to be seen.
questions.explanation: Choose a brightly-colored helmet. It protects you in a crash and helps other drivers see you on the road.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Get as close as possible to the vehicle in front of you.
Not signal your intentions, as that may distract the driver you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the left portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When passing on the left, ride in the left portion of your lane. Signal, check for traffic, and pass when safe. Then signal and return to your original lane.

questions.question: When riding in a group, why should inexperienced riders ride near the front?

options.text: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
They will get lost if they are leading.
They may slow down the group if they lead.
They will ride too fast in any other position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Experienced riders can watch them more easily.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can keep a close eye on them.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:

options.text: Riders who have ridden their motorcycle for less than six months.
Faulty ignition systems.
Distractions caused by passengers.
Riders riding at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders who have ridden their motorcycle for less than six months.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a motorcycle new to you. Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience on their bike.

questions.question: When a group of riders passes another vehicle, they should pass:

options.text: In a staggered formation.
In a pyramid formation.
One at a time.
In a splintered formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: One at a time.
questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders should pass one at a time. The next rider should wait until the first rider safely returns to the original lane before passing. Continue this pattern until all riders have passed.

questions.question: To protect a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Be made of soft material.
Be made of heavy material.
Fit loosely so they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some leg.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or strong synthetic material that cover your legs completely. Your clothing should fit snugly so it does not flap in the wind, but not so tight that it limits your movement.

questions.question: If you find yourself riding next to another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Speed up or slow down.
Wave at the other driver.
Stay alongside the vehicle until the next exit.
Let the other driver worry about it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up or slow down.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous because you may be in its blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if a hazard appears. Speed up or slow down to move away from the vehicle.
